description: Read every 'versioning' entry as a statement about a REGISTRY'S TAG SHAPE, never about the
upstream project's release policy. Renovate has to sort tags to say which is newer, and its
default docker versioning rejects or mis-orders several shapes. A wrong parse does not
error: it silently offers the wrong version, or none. Each rule is the parser that makes
one registry's tags sortable; the tags quoted are shape illustrations, not current
versions.
Release policy (calendar versioning, minors that break) lives in override-calver.json and
override-breaking-changes.json; a regex mapping a segment to 'patch' is a parsing decision,
not a risk grading.
One linuxserver repository carries several tag dialects (e.g. '2.0.0.5344-ls84' beside
'version-' and arch-prefixed variants) which default docker versioning cannot order
(#246). semver-coerced is the lenient parser: it coerces down to major.minor.patch, so a
fourth segment and an '-lsNNN' rebuild counter are invisible to comparison. The manifests
pin the bare three-segment tag plus a digest, so rebuilds arrive as digest refreshes.
lidarr. One bare tag from a retired build-number scheme ('8.1.2135', frozen since 2017)
survives in the registry, and semver-coerced cannot tell it from a release, so it is
offered as an enormous upgrade. The exclusion names exactly that tag; any genuinely new
version stays offerable.
sonarr. The bare tag '5.14' names the Mono runtime of a retired tag dialect
('5.14-<app version>-lsNN'), not a Sonarr release, and semver-coerced reads it as a
future major. The exclusion names exactly that tag; a real release of that line would
carry more segments and stays offerable.
plex. Tags are shaped like '1.43.3.10896-cb3ebc72d': four numeric segments and a git short
sha. Plain semver cannot parse that and 'loose' ordered it unpredictably (#2946). The regex
names the fourth segment 'build' (the segment that actually moves between Plex releases),
so those bumps grade as patches; that grading is a consequence of the mapping, not a
judgement about Plex.
unbound. Tags like '1.25.2-1' are an upstream version plus an IMAGE rebuild counter.
Under semver a trailing '-1' is a PRERELEASE, so the newer rebuild sorts below '1.25.2'
and is never offered; the regex maps that suffix to 'build' instead (#2946). The anchored
pattern also excludes the '-quic' variants and 'latest'/'canary' tags, so only the build
line is considered.
SQL Server. Tags name a year-branded product, a servicing update and an OS base (e.g.
'2022-CU16-ubuntu-22.04'); the year is a REAL product major, not calver. A lenient parser
sorts these strings alphabetically, offering sideways, backwards and preview moves. The
regex orders year/CU/GDR/base numerically (RTM is servicing zero); RC, CTP, '-preview'
and alias tags match nothing and are never offered.
minio, currently DORMANT: disable-updates.json turns minio off. Kept so the pin stays
sortable if minio is re-enabled; deleting it would make re-enablement quietly offer the
wrong tag. Tags like 'RELEASE.2025-01-03T05-34-25Z' are a timestamp with no version in
them; the regex maps year/month/day onto major/minor/patch so tags order. Keep in step
with override-calver.json, which grades those segments as dates, not risk.
dragonfly-operator chart. PROBLEM: Flux rejects a digest in an OCIRepository's ref.tag field,
so the globally-extended docker:pinDigests would produce a manifest Flux refuses to
reconcile. This opts that one chart out of digest pinning; it says nothing about the chart's
versioning.
